articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Recent sightings of five migratory species highlight the ecological importance of the reserve’s forests, grasslands and wetlands
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Recent sightings of five migratory species highlight the ecological importance of the reserve’s forests, grasslands and wetlands
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The arrival of migratory birds from Siberia, Central Asia and other northern regions has brought renewed attention to the ecological significance of Kawal Tiger Reserve (KTR) in the erstwhile combined Adilabad district, with five species recorded in the Jannaram Forest Division and adjoining areas over the past few days. The Siberian Stonechat, Red-headed Bunting, Olive-backed Pipit, Garganey and Northern Pintail were among the winter visitors documented jointly by Jannaram Forest Divisional Officer (FDO) M. Ram Mohan and wildlife researcher and Hyderabad Tiger Conservation Society (HyTiCoS) coordinator Venkat Anagandhula. The sightings, recorded both within and outside the reserve’s forest areas, highlight the importance of Kawal’s diverse habitats in supporting migratory birds. Among the recent arrivals, the Red-headed Bunting (Emberiza bruniceps), a small migratory bird distinguished by its reddish-brown head and yellow body, breeds in Central Asia before migrating to the Indian subcontinent during winter. It generally inhabits open scrublands, grasslands and agricultural fields, feeding on seeds, grains and insects. The Olive-backed Pipit (Anthus hodgsoni), which breeds in the Himalayan region and parts of northern and eastern Asia, migrates southwards during winter. It prefers woodland edges, forest clearings and scrub habitats, where it feeds on insects, small invertebrates and seeds. The Siberian Stonechat (Saxicola maurus), another winter visitor to Telangana, travels from its breeding grounds in Siberia and Central and northern Asia. The species is commonly found in grasslands, scrublands, agricultural fields and wetland edges, feeding primarily on insects. The Garganey (Spatula querquedula) and Northern Pintail (Anas acuta), both migratory dabbling ducks, have also been recorded in the Kawal landscape. These species breed in northern regions and migrate to the Indian subcontinent during winter, seeking freshwater wetlands, reservoirs and shallow water bodies that provide suitable feeding grounds. The Annual Waterbird Census conducted between January 3 and 18, 2026, which covered selected freshwater ecosystems within and around Kawal Tiger Reserve in the erstwhile Adilabad district, documented more than 70 species of waterbirds, including resident birds, winter visitors and passage migrants. The census recorded species such as the Northern Pintail, Common Redshank, Red-crested Pochard, Common Teal, Cotton Pygmy Goose, sandpipers and Temminck’s Stint.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Some migratory birds travel thousands of kilometres to reach their wintering grounds in India, where they generally remain until March before returning to their breeding habitats.

articles.title: Myanmar calls ASEAN review of peace plan 'unfair and imbalanced'; questions bloc's treatment
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila did not reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar has termed the ASEAN leaders' assessment of its implementation of a five-point peace plan "unfair and imbalanced", accusing the regional bloc of disregarding its views and denying it equal rights and representation as a member state. In a statement issued on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila on November 15, 2026 did not adequately reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country. "Although ASEAN has yet to reach a consensus, Myanmar continues to engage bilaterally with individual ASEAN Member states," the Ministry said, expressing appreciation to members that had extended support and assistance in recognition of what it described as positive developments in the country. The statement comes after ASEAN leaders reiterated their concern over insufficient progress in implementing the five-point peace plan agreed upon in April 2021 following the military takeover in Myanmar. They also extended restrictions on the country's leadership attending the bloc's summits, saying the ban would remain until there was meaningful progress in implementing the plan. Under the arrangement, Myanmar can be represented at ASEAN summits only by a non-political representative, such as a career diplomat. The five-point consensus calls for an immediate cessation of violence, dialogue among all parties, an ASEAN special envoy to facilitate mediation, a visit by the envoy to Myanmar to meet all parties, and humanitarian assistance through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management. The conflict in Myanmar has continued since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, triggering widespread protests, a military crackdown and an armed resistance movement. ASEAN's five-point consensus was adopted in April 2021 in an attempt to end the violence and facilitate a peaceful resolution to the crisis. However, the bloc has repeatedly expressed frustration over the lack of progress in its implementation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rejecting criticism of its handling of the conflict, Myanmar said it had continued to cooperate with ASEAN's suggestions and recommendations while safeguarding its national interests and sovereignty.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Myanmar calls ASEAN review of peace plan 'unfair and imbalanced'; questions bloc's treatment

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 06:55:30 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila did not reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar has termed the ASEAN leaders' assessment of its implementation of a five-point peace plan "unfair and imbalanced", accusing the regional bloc of disregarding its views and denying it equal rights and representation as a member state. In a statement issued on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Myanmar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the review and recommendations adopted at the ASEAN Summit in Manila on November 15, 2026 did not adequately reflect the positive measures undertaken by the country. "Although ASEAN has yet to reach a consensus, Myanmar continues to engage bilaterally with individual ASEAN Member states," the Ministry said, expressing appreciation to members that had extended support and assistance in recognition of what it described as positive developments in the country. The statement comes after ASEAN leaders reiterated their concern over insufficient progress in implementing the five-point peace plan agreed upon in April 2021 following the military takeover in Myanmar. They also extended restrictions on the country's leadership attending the bloc's summits, saying the ban would remain until there was meaningful progress in implementing the plan. Under the arrangement, Myanmar can be represented at ASEAN summits only by a non-political representative, such as a career diplomat. The five-point consensus calls for an immediate cessation of violence, dialogue among all parties, an ASEAN special envoy to facilitate mediation, a visit by the envoy to Myanmar to meet all parties, and humanitarian assistance through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management. The conflict in Myanmar has continued since the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, triggering widespread protests, a military crackdown and an armed resistance movement. ASEAN's five-point consensus was adopted in April 2021 in an attempt to end the violence and facilitate a peaceful resolution to the crisis. However, the bloc has repeatedly expressed frustration over the lack of progress in its implementation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rejecting criticism of its handling of the conflict, Myanmar said it had continued to cooperate with ASEAN's suggestions and recommendations while safeguarding its national interests and sovereignty.

Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
Representation (Noun)
प्रतिनिधित्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Representation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Appreciation (Noun)
प्रशंसा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Appreciation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries other than their own have endured hunger, thirst and other deprivations while being detained indefinitely in places with poor human rights records and little oversight. For those expelled to South Sudan, and their families, the ordeal has come at an additional cost. Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones. Instead, the guards pocketed most of the money, families said, while detainees went for days without food or clean water, and months held incommunicado. “They used our desperate situation,” said Ngoc Phan, a U.S. citizen whose husband Tuan Phan had been detained in South Sudan for nearly a year before he was repatriated to Vietnam in June. “If that's not exploitation, I don't know what is.” It is the inevitable outcome, she said, of a U.S. immigration policy that places deportees in the custody of countries struggling with poverty and corruption, then looks the other way. Five deportees remain in custody in South Sudan, a country in East Africa where millions face severe hunger and poverty after years of civil conflict and devastating floods. The economy is in tatters, and government workers rarely receive wages. In all, Ms. Ngoc Phan said she forked over roughly $4,000 intended for food, water and a cellphone. She sent several hundred dollars on multiple occasions and each time, her husband said, guards would give him a few bananas and apples, and some peanuts. Mr. Tuan Phan, 44, said he lost 20 pounds while under confinement at a gated three-story building in Juba, the capital, and that tensions grew between detainees and guards as living conditions worsened. One detainee who wanted a window open for fresh air was struck in the face by a guard, and another who complained about a lack of soap was locked in his room for days and only let out to eat, he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “I feared for my life every day I was there,” he said.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 06:21:00 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries other than their own have endured hunger, thirst and other deprivations while being detained indefinitely in places with poor human rights records and little oversight. For those expelled to South Sudan, and their families, the ordeal has come at an additional cost. Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones. Instead, the guards pocketed most of the money, families said, while detainees went for days without food or clean water, and months held incommunicado. “They used our desperate situation,” said Ngoc Phan, a U.S. citizen whose husband Tuan Phan had been detained in South Sudan for nearly a year before he was repatriated to Vietnam in June. “If that's not exploitation, I don't know what is.” It is the inevitable outcome, she said, of a U.S. immigration policy that places deportees in the custody of countries struggling with poverty and corruption, then looks the other way. Five deportees remain in custody in South Sudan, a country in East Africa where millions face severe hunger and poverty after years of civil conflict and devastating floods. The economy is in tatters, and government workers rarely receive wages. In all, Ms. Ngoc Phan said she forked over roughly $4,000 intended for food, water and a cellphone. She sent several hundred dollars on multiple occasions and each time, her husband said, guards would give him a few bananas and apples, and some peanuts. Mr. Tuan Phan, 44, said he lost 20 pounds while under confinement at a gated three-story building in Juba, the capital, and that tensions grew between detainees and guards as living conditions worsened. One detainee who wanted a window open for fresh air was struck in the face by a guard, and another who complained about a lack of soap was locked in his room for days and only let out to eat, he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “I feared for my life every day I was there,” he said.

✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Confinement (Adjective)
कारावास — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Confinement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

A. Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as gua' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

D. The author contends that 'U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for..." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “I feared for my life every day I was there,” he said.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“I feared for my life every day I was there,” he said." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा, "हर दिन जब मैं वहां रहता था तो मुझे अपनी जान का डर रहता था।")

articles.title: EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The European Union on Sunday (November 22, 2026) rejected a climate deal that omits any mention of fossil fuels , as the UN climate talks in Türkiye pushed into record extra time. Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”. “We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr. O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end. Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale. The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas. “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr. O’Brien. Ahead of the closing session, COP31 President and Türkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum had urged parties to find a compromise, after nearly two weeks of grinding negotiations led to a complete stalemate in the final moments. “We had negotiations and we listened to everyone patiently,” Mr. Kurum told the final plenary. “We wanted to give a good message to the rest of the world.” Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching political agreement to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the EU and island nations threatened by rising seas protested after a proposed text did not mention fossil fuels by name. Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petro-States such as oil-rich Saudi Arabia. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP . Threats of a walkout on Saturday (November 21, 2026) prompted Türkiye and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the EU and Saudi Arabia, but a compromise remained elusive. The latest text introduces an oblique reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels, but stops short of naming them explicitly.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The text also proposed retaining a contentious push to expand carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. Climate campaigners had urged countries to reject the deal. “This text isn’t a climate plan. It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org.

hinglishTracks.en: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — आयरलैंड के जलवायु और ऊर्जा मंत्री दारागह ओ'ब्रायन ने कहा कि यूरोपीय संघ अंताल्या संधि का समर्थन नहीं करेगा, जिसमें "जीवाश्म ईंधन का भी उल्लेख नहीं है", क्योंकि संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु वार्ता रिकॉर्ड अतिरिक्त समय में चली गई।।

hinglishTracks.en: The European Union on Sunday (November 22, 2026) rejected a climate deal that omits any mention of fossil fuels , as the UN climate talks in Türkiye pushed into record extra time.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यूरोपीय संघ ने रविवार (नवंबर 22, 2026) को एक जलवायु समझौते को खारिज कर दिया, जिसमें जीवाश्म ईंधन के किसी भी उल्लेख को छोड़ दिया गया था, क्योंकि तुर्किये में संयुक्त राष्ट्र की जलवायु वार्ता को रिकॉर्ड अतिरिक्त समय में धकेल दिया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — आयरलैंड के जलवायु और ऊर्जा मंत्री दाराग ओ'ब्रायन, जिनका देश यूरोपीय संघ का घूर्णनशील राष्ट्रपति पद संभालता है, ने कहा कि यूरोपीय संघ और उसके सदस्य देश इस समझौते पर "आपत्ति" करते हैं क्योंकि यह "समय के अनुरूप नहीं है"।।

hinglishTracks.en: “We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — "हम किसी कवर निर्णय या अंताल्या संधि का समर्थन नहीं करेंगे, जिसमें जीवाश्म ईंधन का भी उल्लेख नहीं है, जो जलवायु परिवर्तन का प्रमुख चालक है," श्रीमान ने कहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — शिखर सम्मेलन के आधिकारिक समापन के 44 घंटे बाद ओ'ब्रायन ने अराजक समापन सत्र को रिकॉर्ड बताया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — पनामा, जो सीओपी प्रक्रिया का मुखर आलोचक है, जिसने वार्ता से दूर जाने की धमकी दी थी, ने भी प्रस्तावित सौदे पर औपचारिक रूप से आपत्ति जताई, क्योंकि शिखर सम्मेलन हंगामेदार समापन पर पहुंच गया।।

hinglishTracks.en: The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — प्रस्तावित सौदे को लगभग 200 देशों की आम सहमति की आवश्यकता है, लेकिन कई राज्यों ने निराशा व्यक्त की थी कि मसौदे में कोयला, तेल या गैस का उल्लेख नहीं था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Frustration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: निराशा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Frustration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — उन्होंने कहा, ''हम समय से पीछे जाकर बातचीत स्वीकार नहीं करेंगे।।

hinglishTracks.en: And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — और हम ऐसे सीओपी को स्वीकार नहीं करेंगे जो जीवाश्म ईंधन को ग्रीनवॉश करता हो,'' श्री ने कहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: Ahead of the closing session, COP31 President and Türkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum had urged parties to find a compromise, after nearly two weeks of grinding negotiations led to a complete stalemate in the final moments.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — समापन सत्र से पहले, COP31 के अध्यक्ष और तुर्किये के पर्यावरण मंत्री मूरत कुरुम ने पार्टियों से समझौता करने का आग्रह किया था, लगभग दो सप्ताह की तीखी बातचीत के बाद अंतिम क्षणों में पूर्ण गतिरोध पैदा हो गया था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Environmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित। इसके Synonyms हैं: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural और Antonyms हैं: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic।

hinglishTracks.en: “We had negotiations and we listened to everyone patiently,” Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — श्रीमान ने कहा, "हमने बातचीत की और हमने सभी की बात धैर्यपूर्वक सुनी।"।

hinglishTracks.en: Kurum told the final plenary.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — कुरुम ने अंतिम पूर्ण सत्र में बताया।।

hinglishTracks.en: “We wanted to give a good message to the rest of the world.” Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — "हम बाकी दुनिया को एक अच्छा संदेश देना चाहते थे।" जीवाश्म ईंधन जलवायु वार्ता में एक फ्लैशप्वाइंट है, जो ऊर्जा की बढ़ती कीमतों और ईरान में युद्ध से उत्पन्न भू-राजनीतिक तनाव की कठिन पृष्ठभूमि के खिलाफ आता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Geopolitical' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: भू-राजनैतिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Geopolitical' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching political agreement to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — कम उम्मीदों के साथ, वार्ता प्रमुख ऑस्ट्रेलिया ने COP31 में देशों द्वारा सहमत की गई बातों को ध्यान में रखने और जलवायु कार्रवाई के भविष्य के पाठ्यक्रम के बारे में एक संकेत भेजने के लिए एक व्यापक राजनीतिक समझौते की मांग की थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: But the EU and island nations threatened by rising seas protested after a proposed text did not mention fossil fuels by name.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — लेकिन प्रस्तावित पाठ में जीवाश्म ईंधन का नाम लेकर उल्लेख नहीं किए जाने के बाद बढ़ते समुद्र से खतरे में पड़े यूरोपीय संघ और द्वीप राष्ट्रों ने विरोध प्रदर्शन किया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petro-States such as oil-rich Saudi Arabia.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — जीवाश्म ईंधन से जुड़ी भाषा का तेल-समृद्ध सऊदी अरब जैसे पेट्रो-राज्यों द्वारा कड़ा विरोध किया जाता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — एएफपी द्वारा संपर्क किये जाने पर एक सऊदी अधिकारी ने टिप्पणी करने से इनकार कर दिया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Threats of a walkout on Saturday (November 21, 2026) prompted Türkiye and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the EU and Saudi Arabia, but a compromise remained elusive.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — शनिवार (नवंबर 21, 2026) को वाकआउट की धमकियों ने तुर्किये और ऑस्ट्रेलिया को यूरोपीय संघ और सऊदी अरब के बीच जल्दबाजी में बैठक बुलाने के लिए प्रेरित किया, लेकिन कोई समझौता नहीं हो सका।।

hinglishTracks.en: The latest text introduces an oblique reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels, but stops short of naming them explicitly.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — नवीनतम पाठ दुनिया को जीवाश्म ईंधन से दूर स्थानांतरित करने के लिए 2023 में पिछले वैश्विक समझौते का एक परोक्ष संदर्भ प्रस्तुत करता है, लेकिन उन्हें स्पष्ट रूप से नाम देने से रोकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The text also proposed retaining a contentious push to expand carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — पाठ में कार्बन कैप्चर का विस्तार करने के लिए एक विवादास्पद प्रयास को बनाए रखने का भी प्रस्ताव दिया गया है, जो कि जीवाश्म ईंधन उद्योग द्वारा समर्थित तकनीक है, लेकिन उत्सर्जन में कटौती में महंगी और अप्रभावी के रूप में इसकी आलोचना की गई है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Contentious' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: विवादास्पद — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Contentious' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Climate campaigners had urged countries to reject the deal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — जलवायु प्रचारकों ने देशों से इस समझौते को अस्वीकार करने का आग्रह किया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: “This text isn’t a climate plan.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — “यह पाठ कोई जलवायु योजना नहीं है।।

hinglishTracks.en: It’s a licence to keep polluting,” said Sara Shaw of the environmental group 350.org.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — पर्यावरण समूह 350.org की सारा शॉ ने कहा, यह प्रदूषण फैलाते रहने का लाइसेंस है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Environmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित। इसके Synonyms हैं: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural और Antonyms हैं: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic।

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 EU will ‘not endorse’ climate deal, throwing COP31 outcome into doubt

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 06:15:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien said the EU would not back an Antalya Pact that “does not even mention fossil fuels”, as the UN climate talks ran into record extra time

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The European Union on Sunday (November 22, 2026) rejected a climate deal that omits any mention of fossil fuels , as the UN climate talks in Türkiye pushed into record extra time. Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”. “We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr. O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end. Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale. The proposed deal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many States had expressed frustration that the draft did not refer to coal, oil or gas. “We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said Mr. O’Brien. Ahead of the closing session, COP31 President and Türkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum had urged parties to find a compromise, after nearly two weeks of grinding negotiations led to a complete stalemate in the final moments. “We had negotiations and we listened to everyone patiently,” Mr. Kurum told the final plenary. “We wanted to give a good message to the rest of the world.” Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. With expectations low, negotiations chief Australia had sought an overarching political agreement to capture what countries agreed at COP31 and send a signal about the future course of climate action. But the EU and island nations threatened by rising seas protested after a proposed text did not mention fossil fuels by name. Language around fossil fuels is fiercely opposed by petro-States such as oil-rich Saudi Arabia. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP . Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member States “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”. “We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” Mr. O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end. articles.title: Rebels kill 15 in South Sudan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: An official hinted at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An attack on Sunday (November 22, 2026) by rebels in northwestern South Sudan has killed at least 15 civilians, with the toll likely to rise, local sources told AFP . One official pointed the finger at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025. “The attack on the Bol Bol Boma area in Tonj East County, Warrap State, began late on Saturday,” Machuei Bith, the county's caretaker commissioner, told AFP . He blamed the deaths on fighters from neighbouring Unity State belonging to Machar's SPLA-IO armed group. "Fifteen civilians and cattle keepers were killed and four armed attackers with SPLA-IO uniforms were also killed," he told AFP . A local police officer confirmed the story on condition of anonymity and said the fighting was still ongoing on Sunday morning. "Further details on casualties from both sides will be shared later on with the media," the officer said. 23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces Since independence from Sudan in 2011, the world's youngest country has been forced to grapple with various violent conflicts, linked to political infighting, ethnic tensions or competition for resources.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Between 2013 and 2018, the eastern African country was torn apart by a civil war pitting forces loyal to Machar against those supporting Kiir, which left more than 4,00,000 people dead.

📰 Rebels kill 15 in South Sudan

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: An official hinted at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An attack on Sunday (November 22, 2026) by rebels in northwestern South Sudan has killed at least 15 civilians, with the toll likely to rise, local sources told AFP . One official pointed the finger at fighters loyal to the country's former first Vice-President Riek Machar, a longtime rival of President Salva Kiir who has been under house arrest since March 2025. “The attack on the Bol Bol Boma area in Tonj East County, Warrap State, began late on Saturday,” Machuei Bith, the county's caretaker commissioner, told AFP . He blamed the deaths on fighters from neighbouring Unity State belonging to Machar's SPLA-IO armed group. "Fifteen civilians and cattle keepers were killed and four armed attackers with SPLA-IO uniforms were also killed," he told AFP . A local police officer confirmed the story on condition of anonymity and said the fighting was still ongoing on Sunday morning. "Further details on casualties from both sides will be shared later on with the media," the officer said. 23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces Since independence from Sudan in 2011, the world's youngest country has been forced to grapple with various violent conflicts, linked to political infighting, ethnic tensions or competition for resources.

articles.title: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and the 27-nation bloc European Union (EU) are likely to sign the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, an official said. The two sides concluded the negotiations for the pact on January 27 this year. European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force next year. The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules. Under the free trade agreement, described as 'mother of all deals', 93 per cent of Indian shipments will enjoy duty-free access to the 27-nation bloc, while imports of luxury cars and wines from the EU will become less expensive. The deal, concluded after negotiations spanning over two decades, will create a market of about 2 billion people across the world's fourth-largest economy, India, and the second-largest economic bloc, the EU. Watch | India–EU Free Trade Agreement explained: Biggest trade deal in India’s history | India-New Zealand FTA comes into force; new visa categories for Indians, zero-duty access for exports Taken together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and one-third (about USD 11 trillion) of international trade (about $33 trillion). The EU is India's largest trading partner in goods among individual blocs, while India ranks as the EU's ninth-largest goods trading partner globally and sixth in services.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: European Union / India-UK Free Trade Agreement / trade agreements / business (general)

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 16

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 05:09:31 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during PM Modi's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force in 2027

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and the 27-nation bloc European Union (EU) are likely to sign the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, an official said. The two sides concluded the negotiations for the pact on January 27 this year. European Union's Ambassador to India, Jean-Eric Paquet, recently said the FTA will be signed during Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's visit to Brussels in December, and it will come into force next year. The European Commission has already submitted proposals to the Council of the European Union seeking authorisation for signing and conclusion of the agreement, along with the final legal text and tariff schedules. Under the free trade agreement, described as 'mother of all deals', 93 per cent of Indian shipments will enjoy duty-free access to the 27-nation bloc, while imports of luxury cars and wines from the EU will become less expensive. The deal, concluded after negotiations spanning over two decades, will create a market of about 2 billion people across the world's fourth-largest economy, India, and the second-largest economic bloc, the EU. Watch | India–EU Free Trade Agreement explained: Biggest trade deal in India’s history | India-New Zealand FTA comes into force; new visa categories for Indians, zero-duty access for exports Taken together, India and the EU account for 25% of global GDP and one-third (about USD 11 trillion) of international trade (about $33 trillion). The EU is India's largest trading partner in goods among individual blocs, while India ranks as the EU's ninth-largest goods trading partner globally and sixth in services.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: European Union / India-UK Free Trade Agreement / trade agreements / business (general)

articles.title: Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practice successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 05:18:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practice successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Progressive (Adjective)
प्रगतिशील — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Progressive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine." (Hinglish Arth: कादम्बिनी गांगुली ने बाधाओं को तोड़ते हुए पश्चिमी चिकित्सा का अभ्यास करने वाली भारत की पहली महिला चिकित्सकों में से एक बन गईं)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Giving India’s first practicing woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades." articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:48:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare." (Hinglish Arth: इस वर्ष अट्टापडी में बार-बार होने वाली शिशु मृत्यु एक ऐसे संकट की ओर इशारा करती है जो कुपोषण और समय पर स्वास्थ्य देखभाल तक पहुंच से परे है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care." (Hinglish Arth: ग्राउंड ज़ीरो/केरलम/शिशु/स्वास्थ्य/सरकारी स्वास्थ्य देखभाल)

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”. Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia. The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.” The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.” China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.” “Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 12:20:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”. Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia. The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.” The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.” China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.” “Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”. Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia. The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.” The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.” China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.” “Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: China’s Ministry of Commerce in a statement said the new rule would affect the stability of the global semiconductor industry, adding that the U.S. was “misusing export controls to interfere indiscriminately in normal trade cooperation between Chinese enterprises and companies from other countries.” “The U.S. approach runs counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, undermines market rules and the international economic and trade order, and affects the stability of the global semiconductor industry and supply chain,” the statement said.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The episode discuss trends in healthcare expenditure in India, concerns over the regulation of fertility services, the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance, and the impact of environmental and social conditions on public health

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 60th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu looks at key developments in public including healthcare financing, reproductive health, antimicrobial resistance, tuberculosis, environmental exposures and diabetes care. Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, and Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu, discuss the latest National Health Accounts estimates for 2023–24, which show a substantial increase in government health expenditure and a decline in the share of household out-of-pocket spending nationally. The episode also examines the contrasting trends in Keralam, where household healthcare expenditure has increased and the share of government spending has declined. The episode looks at the drug regulator’s direction to pharmaceutical companies to comply with revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs and the potential implications for treatment costs. It also examines concerns over an illegal human egg collection racket in Telangana, including questions about informed consent, women’s safety and the regulation of assisted reproductive technology centres. Developments in Karnataka’s proposed mid-life women’s health programme and mandatory gynaecological check-ups for girls are also discussed. Marking World AMR Awareness Week, the episode explores the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance and the need for appropriate antibiotic use, timely diagnosis, infection prevention and surveillance. It also discusses phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to target bacterial infections, and its potential role in addressing infections that do not respond to conventional antibiotics. The discussion also examines tuberculosis through the lens of social and economic vulnerability, highlighting the importance of nutrition, housing and social support alongside diagnosis and treatment. It looks at the latest figures on domestic funding for India’s TB response, which now accounts for 86% of total spending, even as external funding declines. The discussion also examines the health risks of extreme heat for pregnant women and newborns. A survey of healthcare professionals across five countries found that 98% of Indian clinicians surveyed had treated pregnant women and newborns whose health they believed had been affected by extreme heat. The episode also looks into how fear of diagnosis may discourage people from screening and discusses a Chennai initiative that uses dietary counselling by staff nurses to improve blood sugar control and support long-term diabetes management.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Health Wrap Episode 60 discusses healthcare spending, antimicrobial resistance and more

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:55:05 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The episode discuss trends in healthcare expenditure in India, concerns over the regulation of fertility services, the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance, and the impact of environmental and social conditions on public health

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 60th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu looks at key developments in public including healthcare financing, reproductive health, antimicrobial resistance, tuberculosis, environmental exposures and diabetes care. Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, and Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu, discuss the latest National Health Accounts estimates for 2023–24, which show a substantial increase in government health expenditure and a decline in the share of household out-of-pocket spending nationally. The episode also examines the contrasting trends in Keralam, where household healthcare expenditure has increased and the share of government spending has declined. The episode looks at the drug regulator’s direction to pharmaceutical companies to comply with revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs and the potential implications for treatment costs. It also examines concerns over an illegal human egg collection racket in Telangana, including questions about informed consent, women’s safety and the regulation of assisted reproductive technology centres. Developments in Karnataka’s proposed mid-life women’s health programme and mandatory gynaecological check-ups for girls are also discussed. Marking World AMR Awareness Week, the episode explores the growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance and the need for appropriate antibiotic use, timely diagnosis, infection prevention and surveillance. It also discusses phage therapy, which uses bacteriophages to target bacterial infections, and its potential role in addressing infections that do not respond to conventional antibiotics. The discussion also examines tuberculosis through the lens of social and economic vulnerability, highlighting the importance of nutrition, housing and social support alongside diagnosis and treatment. It looks at the latest figures on domestic funding for India’s TB response, which now accounts for 86% of total spending, even as external funding declines. The discussion also examines the health risks of extreme heat for pregnant women and newborns. A survey of healthcare professionals across five countries found that 98% of Indian clinicians surveyed had treated pregnant women and newborns whose health they believed had been affected by extreme heat. The episode also looks into how fear of diagnosis may discourage people from screening and discusses a Chennai initiative that uses dietary counselling by staff nurses to improve blood sugar control and support long-term diabetes management.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring India’s diverse lentil traditions
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A look at how the humble ingredient travels through different soils, histories, cultures, climates, and kitchens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures. That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says. Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area. Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals. From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / food / food / food and dining (general) / food security / traditional food / India / India / arable farming / Agriculture / agriculture

hinglishTracks.en: From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — मेज पर क्या आता है इसका कोई निश्चित अनुपात नहीं है और हर किसी की माँ का नुस्खा बिल्कुल सही है।।

hinglishTracks.en: From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — ममीदिकाया पप्पू या आम की दाल से लेकर पालक दाल और दाल मखनी तक, देश भर में दालें कैसे तैयार की जाती हैं, इसमें बहुत विविधता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — यहां दाल की गूंज इस तथ्य से परे है कि भारत दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक और दालों का उपभोक्ता है: यह अक्सर घर की याद दिलाता है, जीवन में सरल चीजों की लालसा और संस्कृतियों का संयोजक है।।

hinglishTracks.en: That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हालाँकि, दाल के साथ उस घनिष्ठता का मतलब यह नहीं है कि हर कोई इसे एक ही तरह से बनाता है - या यहाँ तक कि घर में ही इसका स्वाद सबसे अच्छा होता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — 26 साल के हरप्रीत सिंह के लिए, वह हरमंदिर साहिब (स्वर्ण मंदिर) में जो दाल पकाते हैं, वह घर पर पकाई जाने वाली दाल से कहीं बेहतर है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — वह हंसते हुए कहते हैं, ''यह घी ही है जो अंतर पैदा करता है।'' उन्होंने यह भी कहा कि घर पर इसकी राशनिंग होती है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Difference' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: अंतर — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Difference' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — मंदिर में एक क्विंटल दाल में पांच किलो घी मिलाया जाता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — “लेकिन असली रहस्य यह है कि हम दाल को उबालने के बाद, ऊपर से मेल [झाग] हटा देने के बाद सरसों का तेल [सरसों का तेल] मिलाते हैं,” वह कहते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices).
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — सिंह के साथी रसोइये का कहना है कि यह भोर से पहले की प्रार्थना भी है जो देगची (चौड़े मुंह वाले खाना पकाने के बर्तन) में जाती है, जिनमें से कुछ में चार क्विंटल तक दाल रखी जा सकती है, जिसमें 100 किलो प्याज, 24 किलो नमक, 16 किलो अदरक और लहसुन, 6 किलो हल्दी पाउडर और 5 किलो खड़ा मसाला (साबुत मसाले) भी जाते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — रसोई और सेवा क्षेत्र में लाउडस्पीकर पर गुरबानी (धर्मग्रंथों का पाठ) बजती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — अमृतसर का स्वर्ण मंदिर सप्ताह के दिनों में 70,000 से 80,000 लोगों को भोजन कराता है, अमावस्या (अमावस्या) जैसे विशेष सप्ताहांत पर यह संख्या एक लाख से अधिक और गुरु के जन्मदिन पर 2.5 लाख तक हो जाती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — रसोई में, लगभग 450 लोगों की तीन पालियों में, लकड़ी के चूल्हे पर, प्रतिदिन 15-20 क्विंटल दाल पकाई जाती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — यहां की सबसे लोकप्रिय दाल मिश्रित किस्म की है, जिसे छह घंटे तक उबाला जाता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — लंगर में, एक निःशुल्क सामुदायिक भोजन कक्ष जो कई कमरों में फैला हुआ है और एक समय में 3,000 लोगों के बैठने की क्षमता रखता है, दाल एक प्रमुख भोजन है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — सिंह कहते हैं, ''हर कोई इसे खाकर खुश होता है।'' उन्होंने कहा कि लोग अस्पतालों में मरीजों के लिए बर्तनों में खाना भी पैक करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — भारत की पूर्व क्रिकेट कप्तान हरमनप्रीत कौर की भारत के लिए खेलते समय दाल और चावल के शौकीन होने से लेकर, लोकसभा सांसद महुआ मोइत्रा द्वारा संसद में अपने घर की बनी दाल और भिंडी लाने और राष्ट्रपति भवन में परोसी जाने वाली धीमी-पकी, स्वादिष्ट दाल रायसीना तक, दाल ने सामाजिक और पाक संबंधी विभाजनों को तोड़ दिया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Parliament' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संसद — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Parliament' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।
