🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 One country, hundreds of dal recipes: exploring India’s diverse lentil traditions

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:47:18 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A look at how the humble ingredient travels through different soils, histories, cultures, climates, and kitchens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures. That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says. Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area. Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals. From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / food / food / food and dining (general) / food security / traditional food / India / India / arable farming / Agriculture / agriculture

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: From Rajasthan in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, from Kashmir in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, India does dal in thousands of ways. There are no fixed proportions to what comes to the table, and everyone’s mother’s recipe is just right. From mamidikaya pappu , or mango dal , to palak dal and dal makhani , there is great diversity in how lentils are prepared across the country. Dal’s resonance here goes beyond the fact that India is the world’s largest producer and consumer of pulses: it is often a reminder of home, a longing for the simple things in life, and a connector of cultures. That intimacy with dal , however, does not mean everyone makes it the same way — or even that home is where it tastes best. For Harpreet Singh, 26, the dal he cooks at the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) is far better than what is cooked at home. “It’s the ghee that makes the difference,” he says with a laugh, adding that at home, it is rationed. At the temple, five kilos of ghee are added to a quintal of dal . “But the real secret is that we add sarson ka tel [mustard oil] once the dal is boiled, after the mail [froth] on top has been skimmed off,” he says. Singh’s companion cook adds that it is also the pre-dawn prayers that go into the degchis (wide-mouthed cooking pots) , some of which can hold up to four quintals of dal , which also takes 100 kg of onion, 24 kg of salt, 16 kg of ginger and garlic each, 6 kg of turmeric powder, and 5 kg of khada masala (whole spices). The gurbani (reading of the scriptures) plays on a loudspeaker through the kitchens and service area. Amritsar’s Golden Temple feeds 70,000 to 80,000 people on weekdays, with the number going to over a lakh on special weekends like amavasya (new moon), and up to 2.5 lakh on a guru’s birthday. In the kitchen, three shifts of about 450 people cook 15-20 quintals of dal daily, over wood-fired stoves. The most popular dal dish here is the mixed variety, which is boiled for six hours. In the langar , a free communal dining hall spread across several rooms and capable of seating 3,000 people at a time, dal is a staple. “Everyone is happy eating it,” says Singh, adding that people also pack food in vessels for patients in hospitals. From former India cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur’s fondness for dal and rice while playing for India, to Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra bringing her home-cooked dal and bhindi to Parliament, and the slow-cooked, indulgent Dal Raisina served at Rashtrapati Bhavan, dal cuts across social and culinary divides. It is one of India’s most unassuming yet enduring staples — everyday comfort food that can be as humble or elaborate as the occasion demands.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery. It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary. “The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said. “While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added. 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery. It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary. “The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said. “While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added. He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December. “The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted. ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:00:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: Ex-U.K. PM Theresa May tells successor to ‘move on’ from Brexit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Former British Prime Minister Theresa May said she was “aghast” that Prime Minister Andy Burnham could be considering rejoining the European Union, after he sealed trade and youth mobility deals in Brussels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ms. May’s remarks came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials on Friday (November 20, 2026) sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease trade and youth mobility. A decade after Britain narrowly voted to leave the bloc, Mr. Burnham has re-energised talk of closer ties ahead of a government 10-year plan for the U.K., set to be unveiled next month. Ms. May warned that negotiations with the EU risked taking up vast amounts of government time, hampering efforts to tackle other issues. “And that’s one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU,” she said. Ms. May, who supported remaining in the 27-member bloc, said government had to respect the result of the 2016 referendum. “When I became prime minister, I was very clear. People have voted for Brexit. We should deliver Brexit,” she told BBC television. “He (Burnham) wants to pat them (voters) on their head and say ‘you know what? Remember that vote? Well you got it wrong, didn’t you? So have another go and come up with the right answer’,” she said. Ms. May was forced to quit in May 2019 after failing to get her Brexit deal through parliament. “My message to him (Burnham) really is: People voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on,” she added. Mr. Burnham, who has been in office since July 2026, has committed to his predecessor Keir Starmer’s “red lines” on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement. But pro-Brexit campaigners fear he will push at some point to rejoin the 27-nation grouping. Europe Minister Hamish Falconer said the world had changed since 2016, and the U.K. needed to “think over the long term about our relationship with Europe”. “That’s why the prime minister is going to set out more next month as part of the 10-year plan about the long-term relationship between the UK and the EU,” he told Sky News . But he insisted the British people “are going to be the boss of every stage of this”. “We are talking, as the prime minister was clear, about the long term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Following Mr. Burnham’s EU deals, legislation to allow the U.K. to align with certain EU rules, including on food standards, is due to be introduced in parliament this week.

Europe Minister Hamish Falconer said the world had changed since 2016, and the U.K. needed to “think over the long term about our relationship with Europe”. “That’s why the prime minister is going to set out more next month as part of the 10-year plan about the long-term relationship between the UK and the EU,” he told Sky News . But he insisted the British people “are going to be the boss of every stage of this”. “We are talking, as the prime minister was clear, about the long term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Following Mr. Burnham’s EU deals, legislation to allow the U.K. to align with certain EU rules, including on food standards, is due to be introduced in parliament this week.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Ex-U.K. PM Theresa May tells successor to ‘move on’ from Brexit

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:00:25 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Former British Prime Minister Theresa May said she was “aghast” that Prime Minister Andy Burnham could be considering rejoining the European Union, after he sealed trade and youth mobility deals in Brussels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ms. May’s remarks came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials on Friday (November 20, 2026) sealed deals at a Brussels summit to ease trade and youth mobility. A decade after Britain narrowly voted to leave the bloc, Mr. Burnham has re-energised talk of closer ties ahead of a government 10-year plan for the U.K., set to be unveiled next month. Ms. May warned that negotiations with the EU risked taking up vast amounts of government time, hampering efforts to tackle other issues. “And that’s one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU,” she said. Ms. May, who supported remaining in the 27-member bloc, said government had to respect the result of the 2016 referendum. “When I became prime minister, I was very clear. People have voted for Brexit. We should deliver Brexit,” she told BBC television. “He (Burnham) wants to pat them (voters) on their head and say ‘you know what? Remember that vote? Well you got it wrong, didn’t you? So have another go and come up with the right answer’,” she said. Ms. May was forced to quit in May 2019 after failing to get her Brexit deal through parliament. “My message to him (Burnham) really is: People voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on,” she added. Mr. Burnham, who has been in office since July 2026, has committed to his predecessor Keir Starmer’s “red lines” on Europe for this parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement. But pro-Brexit campaigners fear he will push at some point to rejoin the 27-nation grouping. Europe Minister Hamish Falconer said the world had changed since 2016, and the U.K. needed to “think over the long term about our relationship with Europe”. “That’s why the prime minister is going to set out more next month as part of the 10-year plan about the long-term relationship between the UK and the EU,” he told Sky News . But he insisted the British people “are going to be the boss of every stage of this”. “We are talking, as the prime minister was clear, about the long term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Following Mr. Burnham’s EU deals, legislation to allow the U.K. to align with certain EU rules, including on food standards, is due to be introduced in parliament this week.

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies. Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026). A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow him to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Mr. Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Mr. Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, also reiterated on Saturday (November 21, 2026) his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances”. On Saturday (November 21, 2026), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying Mr. Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu. Among other things, it demands an end to “all personal attacks and incitement to hatred” targeting the outgoing Prime Minister and his government. It also called for bringing together “all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people”, without the participation of Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to his remaining in power.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, and a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:58:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies. Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026). A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow him to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Mr. Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Mr. Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, also reiterated on Saturday (November 21, 2026) his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances”. On Saturday (November 21, 2026), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying Mr. Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu. Among other things, it demands an end to “all personal attacks and incitement to hatred” targeting the outgoing Prime Minister and his government. It also called for bringing together “all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people”, without the participation of Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to his remaining in power.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, and a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Likud laid down conditions for a unity government, including no Arab parties and rejection of a Palestinian state, while Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies. Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026). A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority. His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud. Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow him to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Mr. Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Mr. Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. His ally, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, also reiterated on Saturday (November 21, 2026) his refusal to join a coalition with “Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances”. On Saturday (November 21, 2026), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying Mr. Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu. Among other things, it demands an end to “all personal attacks and incitement to hatred” targeting the outgoing Prime Minister and his government. It also called for bringing together “all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people”, without the participation of Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to his remaining in power.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, and a compromise on conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.

articles.title: Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S. media reported, after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive and a 14% fall in Nvidia shares on Friday (November 20, 2026)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company. Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported. The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang. Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully. Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure. The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:37:04 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S. media reported, after Jensen Huang’s resignation as chief executive and a 14% fall in Nvidia shares on Friday (November 20, 2026)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported on Saturday (November 21, 2026), citing people briefed on the confidential investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported on the investigation earlier this week, although it was unable to establish its precise focus. The probe could end without any charges being brought against the company. Questions about Nvidia’s financial disclosures have intensified amid scrutiny of its dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company investigated by American authorities over suspected shipments of restricted AI chips to China. Nvidia last year changed how it reported sales by geographical location, switching from customers’ billing addresses to the countries where they are headquartered, U.S. media reported. The change removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown, despite the company’s significant business there. It remains unclear whether the SEC investigation is connected to those accounting changes or to the scandal surrounding former chief executive Jensen Huang. Mr. Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of working for Beijing. China has denied the espionage allegations, while Megaspeed has maintained that it operates lawfully. Nvidia’s board has appointed former chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive, and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure. The upheaval has shaken investor confidence in one of the world’s most valuable companies, whose advanced semiconductors have been central to the global AI boom. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Friday (November 20, 2026), bringing their losses for the week to more than 20%.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: U.S. President Donald Trump nevertheless called on Friday (November 20, 2026) for Mr. Huang to be reinstated. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Mr. Trump told reporters. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.

Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Investigation (Adjective / Verb)
जाँच पड़ताल — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Investigation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

बुद्धिमत्ता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Intelligence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Confidential (Adjective)
गोपनीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Confidential' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepenin' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepe' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepe' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry is in its early stages, U.S." (Hinglish Arth: प्रतिभूति और विनिमय आयोग की जांच अपने प्रारंभिक चरण में है, यू.एस.)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Nvidia faces U.S. accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return, saying board directors unanimously accepted his resignation." (Hinglish Arth: लेकिन एनवीडिया के चेयरमैन हार्वे जोन्स ने उनकी वापसी से इनकार करते हुए कहा कि बोर्ड निदेशकों ने सर्वसम्मति से उनका इस्तीफा स्वीकार कर लिया है।)

articles.title: Indian science needs fewer borders
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located. There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism. Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal. Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — आधुनिक विज्ञान उचित ही स्वतंत्र जांच पर गर्व करता है, चाहे जांचकर्ता कहीं भी स्थित हो।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Irrespective' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Irrespective' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ऐसा कोई कारण नहीं है कि भारत के बाहर के किसी व्यक्ति का मूल्यांकन उपनिवेशवाद माना जाए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.en: Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — फिर भी प्रधान मंत्री की आर्थिक सलाहकार परिषद में क्रमशः सदस्य, संयुक्त निदेशक और एक युवा पेशेवर, संजीव सान्याल, सात्विक देव और पायल शर्मा द्वारा व्यापक रूप से बहस किए गए लेख में यह आरोप लगाया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — शोधकर्ता एक अध्ययन लिखते हैं और इसे एक पांडुलिपि के रूप में एक पत्रिका में जमा करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — पत्रिका के संपादक पांडुलिपि का मूल्यांकन करते हैं और इसे क्षेत्र के अन्य विशेषज्ञों को भेजते हैं और पूछते हैं कि क्या काम प्रकाशन लायक है, या इसे संशोधित करने या अस्वीकार करने की आवश्यकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यदि जर्नल पेपर को स्वीकार कर लेता है, तो इसे प्रकाशित किया जाएगा, दुनिया भर के वैज्ञानिकों के ध्यान में लाया जाएगा और इसका एक स्थायी रिकॉर्ड संरक्षित किया जाएगा।।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Indian science needs fewer borders

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:51:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located. There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism. Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal. Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administrative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administrative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Irrespective (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Irrespective' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Indian science needs fewer borders", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Indian science needs fewer borders' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Indian science needs fewer borders' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Indian science needs fewer borders' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and..." (Hinglish Arth: अनुसंधान संस्थानों को समय पर वित्त पोषण, बेहतर शिक्षण प्रोत्साहन, अधिक स्वायत्तता, नेतृत्व नियंत्रण, बदले की भावना के खिलाफ सुरक्षा उपाय और कम प्रशासनिक बोझ की आवश्यकता है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Indian science needs fewer borders"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved." (Hinglish Arth: यदि जर्नल पेपर को स्वीकार कर लेता है, तो इसे प्रकाशित किया जाएगा, दुनिया भर के वैज्ञानिकों के ध्यान में लाया जाएगा और इसका एक स्थायी रिकॉर्ड संरक्षित किया जाएगा।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / France / space programme / defence equipment / Artificial Intelligence / economy / security measures / United Nations / technology (general) / oceans / climate change / ISRO / water / summit / weather science / science (general) / law

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Thumba to Kourou, over 60 years of space partnership

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:32:41 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / France / space programme / defence equipment / Artificial Intelligence / economy / security measures / United Nations / technology (general) / oceans / climate change / ISRO / water / summit / weather science / science (general) / law

Cooperation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.title: Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:15:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Conservative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conservative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Achievement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Progressive (Adjective)
प्रगतिशील — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Progressive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine." (Hinglish Arth: कादम्बिनी गांगुली ने बाधाओं को तोड़ते हुए पश्चिमी चिकित्सा का अभ्यास करने वाली भारत की पहली महिला चिकित्सकों में से एक बन गईं)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades." (Hinglish Arth: चिकित्सा और सामाजिक क्षेत्र में उनके योगदान को पूर्ण मान्यता बहुत बाद में, हाल के दशकों में ही मिली।)

articles.title: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

hinglishTracks.en: However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:50:32 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 01:36:34 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears. Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026. Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor. “We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district. Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. B. Ground Zero / Keralam / infants / health / government health care.

articles.title: Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With a view to developing a scientific temperament among students and the general public, state-of-the-art “digital planetariums and education centres” will be established in all the divisions of the state, Bihar Science and Technology Minister Sheela Kumari said on Friday (November 20, 2026). “The district magistrates of the districts concerned have been requested to provide a minimum of two acres of land for the purpose,” Ms. Kumari said while addressing a press conference in Patna. These centres will provide children and young people with practical knowledge of astronomy and space research, she said, while praising Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s leadership for the initiative. In reply to a query, she said that these planetariums will be ready in a year. The Minister further stated that digital planetariums/space and astronomy education centres will also be established in three districts—East Champaran, Jamui, and Purnea—as part of the Union Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture and Science (SPOCS). “The total estimated project cost is ₹39.00 crore, which will be funded with central assistance,” she said, adding that the target is to commence construction work during the current financial year, 2026-27. A digital planetarium uses computer software and high-resolution digital projectors (or LED panels) to display 3D simulations of the night sky, space travel, and science visuals inside a dome theatre. Unlike traditional optical-mechanical projectors that only show fixed star positions, digital systems can fly viewers through galaxies, simulate different time periods, and play full-dome films. Ms. Kumari was accompanied by Department Secretary Himanshu Sharma and a host of other senior officials during the press conference. In order to generate public interest in science and technology, efforts are also being made to operate mobile science exhibition buses, observatory domes, and astro parks through the National Council of Science Museums.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Notably, the state currently has two functional planetariums—one each in Patna and Darbhanga. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 04:04:58 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With a view to developing a scientific temperament among students and the general public, state-of-the-art “digital planetariums and education centres” will be established in all the divisions of the state, Bihar Science and Technology Minister Sheela Kumari said on Friday (November 20, 2026). “The district magistrates of the districts concerned have been requested to provide a minimum of two acres of land for the purpose,” Ms. Kumari said while addressing a press conference in Patna. These centres will provide children and young people with practical knowledge of astronomy and space research, she said, while praising Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s leadership for the initiative. In reply to a query, she said that these planetariums will be ready in a year. The Minister further stated that digital planetariums/space and astronomy education centres will also be established in three districts—East Champaran, Jamui, and Purnea—as part of the Union Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture and Science (SPOCS). “The total estimated project cost is ₹39.00 crore, which will be funded with central assistance,” she said, adding that the target is to commence construction work during the current financial year, 2026-27. A digital planetarium uses computer software and high-resolution digital projectors (or LED panels) to display 3D simulations of the night sky, space travel, and science visuals inside a dome theatre. Unlike traditional optical-mechanical projectors that only show fixed star positions, digital systems can fly viewers through galaxies, simulate different time periods, and play full-dome films. Ms. Kumari was accompanied by Department Secretary Himanshu Sharma and a host of other senior officials during the press conference. In order to generate public interest in science and technology, efforts are also being made to operate mobile science exhibition buses, observatory domes, and astro parks through the National Council of Science Museums.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Notably, the state currently has two functional planetariums—one each in Patna and Darbhanga. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.

Construction (Noun)
निर्माण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Construction' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Appointment (Adjective)
नियुक्ति — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Appointment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Polytechnic (Adjective)
नानायंत्र — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Polytechnic' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Digital planetariums, education centres will be ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Digital planetariums, education centres will ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Digital planetariums, education centres will ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC." A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: BJP’s invitation to Pakistan’s Minister vindicates Abdullah’s stance: J&K Deputy Chief Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that the BJP-led government’s move to invite Pakistan’s Minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue Forum “vindicated the stand of National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah and vice president Omar Abdullah.” Referring to the BJP’s stance after the 2025 Pahalgam attack, Mr. Choudhary said, “The BJP will say it will not talk to Pakistan. And when Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah advocate dialogue, the BJP will call them Pakistani. I want to ask the BJP: hasn’t a Pakistani Minister been invited to India on their invitation?” He said the invitation to the Pakistani Minister proved that “the stance of my leaders was right then and is right now.” “The NC’s stance is the same as the one articulated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who would say, ‘You can choose your friends, but you cannot choose your neighbours.’ One must always maintain good relations with one’s neighbours,” said Mr. Choudhary. Asking Pakistan to end terrorism, Mr. Choudhary said, “Both Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah have been asking Pakistan to end terrorism and close terror camps if Pakistan wants better relations. We stand behind our leaders.” People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The two countries share a common history and several mutual concerns, including political issues, climate change, and water-related matters, which can only be addressed through engagement and dialogue. Hostility and non-engagement cannot resolve these issues. Both countries should come to the table and resume dialogue for peace and development in the subcontinent,” he said.

📰 BJP’s invitation to Pakistan’s Minister vindicates Abdullah’s stance: J&K Deputy Chief Minister
